issues.body: The quotient deliberately maps IRIs without an extractable scheme://authority (for example urn:isbn:123 and relative IRIs) to QuotientTerm::OpaqueIri containing the complete original IRI. Nevertheless, the module threat model says a summary does not reveal individual IRIs because they are collapsed to authority. The README and MPC skill repeat that unqualified claim. A published summary can therefore disclose an individual opaque IRI verbatim, contradicting the privacy/leakage description on this MPC-adjacent surface.
issues.fix_hint: State consistently in quotient.rs, README.md, and skills/mpc/SKILL.md that authority-bearing IRIs are collapsed, but authority-less/relative IRIs are retained verbatim and disclosed. Alternatively, change the quotient to map such IRIs to a non-identifying common class, then add a recall-safety test for joins and bound constants involving opaque IRIs.
issues.title: Threat model falsely claims summaries never reveal individual IRIs

verdict.summary: Round 1's selection-alignment and arithmetic-overflow findings are addressed with fail-closed validation, checked multiplication, and focused regressions. However, the new public documentation makes a privacy-sensitive claim that the representation does not uphold: IRIs without an extractable authority are stored verbatim as OpaqueIri, while several threat-model passages say individual IRIs are not revealed. Because this is a newly identified honesty issue on an MPC-adjacent surface, progress is regressing.
